concerns.location: Assumptions: Public datasets (NIST, UCI, OpenML) contain sufficient samples (≥50) with measured residual stress...
concerns.text: The core research question (quantifying the mediating impact of residual stress) requires real measured‑stress observations. The spec assumes such datasets exist, yet no publicly available fatigue dataset with measured residual stress is known; the plan would fall back to synthetic data, which cannot provide empirical evidence for mediation or added predictive value.

Feature Set B adds an estimated residual‑stress proxy that is a deterministic linear function of existing process parameters (σ_res ≈ k·heat_input·cooling_rate). Comparing Model B to Model A therefore tests a model that includes a feature mathematically derived from the same predictors, creating a circular validation. Any observed performance gain cannot be attributed to “stress‑mediated information” but merely to re‑expressing existing variables, violating independence between predictor and validation target.

The proxy formula is presented as a ‘published empirical correlation’ but lacks any citation, unit specification, or dimensional justification. Without a validated source, the proxy’s construct validity is unsubstantiated, making downstream analyses that rely on it (Feature Set C, construct‑validity check FR‑014) methodologically unsound.
